# SEO / AEO 实操蓝图：站内内容架构

- 作者：Sebastien（@sebastien_t_）
- 发布时间：2026-10-06 20:20（北京时间）
- 原帖：https://x.com/sebastien_t_/status/2107445937698197617
- 原文标题（网页显示）：7 years of SEO/AEO, one blueprint: unlock free traffic from Google and AI answers (Part 1, on-site)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。文中数据、观点及推广内容均为作者表述，未经独立验证。

---

![原文配图](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-封面.jpg)

## 中文全文

下面是我现在用来为自己的网站获取免费自然流量的蓝图，流量来自 Google 和 AI 回答。第一部分讲站内，接下来的第二部分讲站外。

在做 IZeat 之前，我在自己搭建的网站上做了大约 7 年 SEO 和 AEO：3 个垂直领域电商网站、1 个 SaaS 和 1 个博客。

如今，我和 Laetitia 正在打造 IZeat，一款五星级厨师卡路里追踪工具：它会根据你当天剩余的热量额度推荐让人吃得满足的餐食，你只需通过 ChatGPT、Claude 或其他任何助手用一句话记录自己吃了什么。我们在开普敦开发它，团队只有我们两人，还有每天与我们一起工作的智能体 Claude Code 和 Codex。这些智能体撰写了我们大量的公开页面：一个包含 3 个支柱主题、66 篇文章的博客，以及一个包含 113 个词条的术语表。

因此问题变了。不再是“我如何写出一篇能获得排名的页面？”，而是“两个智能体如何以同样的方式撰写每一个页面，同时面向 Google 和 AI 助手（AEO，即答案引擎优化，让页面成为助手引用的来源），以及这套方法如何在下一个栏目或另一个网站上继续奏效？”

这是第一部分，介绍发生在你自己网站上的一切，分为四个部分。

# 想登上 Google 首页？这里是可以遵循的完整站内架构

## 用 7 个步骤搭建架构

[![图片](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-正文-007-1.jpg)](https://x.com/sebastien_t_/article/2107445937698197617/media/2107434747441897472)

1 个中心页和 3 个支柱页

1. **收集。** 从真实且注明日期的来源收集带有搜索量和难度数据的关键词，再加上人们向助手提出的问题。
2. **按意图分组。** 需求相同、搜索结果大体相同，就归到一个页面；需求或内容形式不同，就分别建页面。
3. **选择支柱主题。** 选择需求足够大、且包含足够多不同子主题的宽泛主题。用一行说明每个主题的选择理由。
4. **建立树状结构。** 中心页 → 支柱页 → 主题集群 → 文章。中心页提供导航，支柱页独立回答其主题并引导读者深入了解，主题集群概括一种细分意图，文章回答一个具体问题。每个页面都有对应层级和模板。
5. **分配。** 每个关键词和每个问题都必须且只能有一个负责页面，或者明确给出“暂缓”或“不在范围内”的理由。下一部分会详细讲这一点。
6. **建立链接。** 支柱页链接到文章，文章链回支柱页；文章之间建立同级链接；支柱主题之间建立桥接链接，并使用有描述性的锚文本。这些内部链接会告诉 Google 页面之间的关系。
7. **确定优先级。** 按需求、难度和你能够补充的内容安排写作顺序。

[![图片](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-正文-009-1.jpg)](https://x.com/sebastien_t_/article/2107445937698197617/media/2107435586898300928)

更细致地看一个支柱主题内的内容层级链接。

两条规则贯穿始终：绝不编造指标（缺失值不等于零）；只有当每个重要查询都有对应页面或经过论证的决定时，这棵树才算完成。

[![图片](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-正文-011-1.jpg)](https://x.com/sebastien_t_/article/2107445937698197617/media/2107436095319248896)

更细致地看一个支柱主题内的内部链接。

## 写作前先填写页面规划表

智能体写下任何文字之前，先填写六项：

- 目标：主关键词、关键词变体、由该页面负责的问题。
- 读者任务：“对于［读者］，这个页面让他们能够［完成任务］。”
- 答案：用一两句话给出答案。
- 独有信息：只有这个页面能提供什么。你的数据、有出处的数据、完整示例或经过验证的方法。
- 内容块：页面模板中的每个内容块各写一行。
- 链接：上级页面、更深入的页面、下一步行动。

如果你不加要求，智能体会跳过的那一项就是独有信息。对我们来说，那是 IZeat 自己提供的、注明来源的每 100 克营养数据，读者无法从下一条搜索结果中获得。

## 按一条规则填写每种内容块

模板规定一个页面有哪些内容块。这套方法为每种内容块规定一条规则，不管它属于哪个页面：

- 标题、H1、描述、URL：体现这个查询的主题和承诺。不要承诺页面无法提供的内容。
- 开篇（导语、第一段或定义）：立即回答主要问题。定义即使被单独引用，也必须准确易懂。
- H2 和 H3：按顺序列出读者的次级问题。
- 独有信息：每个数据旁边都标明来源、日期和适用范围。

# 排不上名？你的页面可能在互相竞争。如何解决

当你的两个页面回答同一个搜索问题时，Google 必须从中选择一个，而且常常两个页面的排名都不好。SEO 从业者把这称为关键词蚕食。使用 AI 智能体时，这种情况发生得很快：两个智能体在不同的两天里，很可能分别为同一个查询写出两个页面，而单独看每个页面都没有问题。

阻止这种情况的规则就是第 5 步：每个关键词和每个问题只分配给一个负责页面。任何页面都不回答另一个页面负责的问题。

三件事确保这条规则能够执行：

- 一张统一的归属表。每个关键词占一行，只对应一个页面。我们使用共享电子表格；智能体写作前会读取它，其他文档不复制这张表。
- 一项拒绝重复的检查。每篇文章声明自己的关键词；如果两篇文章声明了同一个关键词，测试就会失败。我们第一次在博客上运行这项检查时，发现了 8 处此前漏掉的重复。
- 即使重复已经发生，也要作出一个决定。在 Search Console 中发现两个页面对应同一个查询时：合并它们，或按意图拆分，让每个页面回答不同的需求。

# 大语言模型不引用你？你的内容结构可能不适合它们。可以遵循的简单规则

助手会把页面切分成段落，并引用其中回答问题的部分。一段写着“如上所示”的内容无法单独引用；带有单位的表格则可以。

| 需求 | 结构 |
| --- | --- |
| 比较选项、给出数量 | 真正的表格：表头注明单位，每个单元格一个数值，下方标明来源，绝不用图片代替 |
| 说明操作流程 | 有序列表，每一步只包含一个动作 |
| 列举或总结 | 项目符号列表，每一项都是能够独立理解的句子 |
| 给出术语的基本信息 | 定义列表：公式、单位、典型范围、来源 |
| 回答问题 | 以问题作为标题，第一句话直接回答 |
| 每个章节 | 能够独立理解的段落，明确写出主题名称，而不是使用“它” |

接下来是 JSON-LD。它让我们困惑的时间比我愿意承认的还要长。每个页面在 head 中放一个代码块，描述页面及其主要主题。并不是每张表格放一个代码块。

只有少数可见内容块在其中有对应项：常见问题（FAQPage）、食谱步骤（HowToStep）、营养表（NutritionInformation）、精选列表（ItemList）、面包屑导航（BreadcrumbList）。普通表格和列表没有对应项。引擎直接从 HTML 中读取它们，这正是可见结构重要的原因。

还有一条黄金法则：JSON-LD 只描述可见内容。页面上没有可见问题，就不要使用 FAQPage；没有真实评分，就不要写评分。Google 表示，要出现在 AI Overviews 中不需要特殊标记；基础要求与普通搜索相同。

# 做完这些还是没有排名？你可能遵循的是规则，而不是读者需求

这正是我犯错的地方。我们让智能体遵守的两条规则来自自己的设计文档，两条都声称是在模仿 Webflow：“术语表词条写 250 个词，像 Webflow 一样”，以及“两句话的导语，第二句提到 IZeat”。这些是从知名网站照搬来的限制，而不是对读者需求的回答。智能体不会质疑这样的规则，它会把规则执行 52 次。

所以，10 月 5 日，我们只使用免费工具，让 Claude 操作 Chrome，进行了统计。

| 术语表 | 抽样词条数 | 长度中位数 | 开篇 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Webflow | 100 | 134 个词，无小标题 | 约 41 个词 |
| Ahrefs | 40 | 约 600 个词，有 H2 标题 | 约 38 个词 |
| HubSpot | 40 | 约 840 个词 | 约 56 个词 |
| IZeat | — | 约 258 个词 | — |

Webflow 的术语表词条并不是 250 个词。而且不存在唯一正确的长度：这三个网站的共同点，是开篇简短，先给出定义。

至于文章开篇，在抽样的 60 篇 Webflow 文章中，有 49 篇的导语只有一句话（中位数为 23 个词），第二句话提到 Webflow 的只有 1 篇。Healthline、Ahrefs、HubSpot 和 Zapier 很少使用导语；它们的第一段有 26–34 个词。我们当时的 52 篇文章全部在导语中提到了 IZeat，导语中位数为 59 个词，包含两到四句话。我们照搬了一种根本不存在的模式。

取代那两条规则的是读者需求。开篇先回答问题。页面需要多长，就由问题本身决定，不设字数要求。只有当 IZeat 有助于回答读者的问题时，导语才提到 IZeat。

在 AEO 方面，我们对 Google AI Overviews 做了一次小样本调查（4 个问题，13 个被引用页面）：第一段长度的中位数约为 47 个词，只有 13 个页面中的 3 个在开头提到品牌，页面总长度约为 1,000 个词。页面类型随问题而变化：“什么是 TDEE”对应计算器，“最佳卡路里追踪应用”对应榜单文章和应用主页，“高蛋白餐食”对应食谱合集。

13 个页面只是一个样本，不是一条定律。被引用的内容反映了当下的竞争情况：如果没有人发布结构化且有来源的数据，那么引用结果中没有这类数据并不能证明什么。有一项外部研究支持了我们的决策方向：GEO 论文（Aggarwal 等，KDD 2024）发现，加入统计数据、引语和引用来源，可以将生成式回答中的可见度提高约 22–41%，而堆砌关键词没有帮助。这是在研究型引擎上进行的对照实验，并不是对任何商业助手的测量。

还有一个错误，这次是我们自己的：我们的方法文件第一版有 2,400 个词，而我说不清它增加了什么价值。重写时，我反复追问三个问题：“这和页面模板有什么区别？”“为什么我们衡量 AEO 而不衡量 SEO？”“JSON-LD 是每页一个还是每张表一个？”现在它大约有 1,400 个词。

第二部分讲站外：发生在你自己网站之外的一切。

如果你使用 Claude Code 或 Codex 来开发：你的智能体现在把自己的方法存放在哪里？

## 英文原文

Here's the blueprint I now use to drive free organic traffic to my websites, from Google and from AI answers. Part 1 is on-site. Part 2, off-site, comes next.

Before IZeat, I did SEO and AEO for about 7 years on sites I built myself: 3 niche e-commerce sites, 1 SaaS and 1 blog.

Today Laetitia and I build IZeat, the five-star chef calorie tracker: it suggests satisfying meals that fit what you have left today, and you log what you ate in one sentence, from ChatGPT, Claude or any other assistant. We build it from Cape Town, the two of us plus the agents we work with every day, Claude Code and Codex. Those agents write a lot of our public pages: a blog of 66 articles under 3 pillars, and a glossary of 113 entries.

So the question changed. It's no longer "how do I write a page that can rank?" It's "how do two agents write every page the same way, for Google and for AI assistants (AEO: answer engine optimisation, being the page an assistant quotes), and how does the method still work on the next section, or on another site?"

This is Part 1, everything that happens on your own site, in four parts.

# Want to be on Google's first page? Here's the full on-site architecture to follow

## Build the architecture in 7 steps

![原文配图](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-正文-007-1.jpg)

1 Hub and 3 Pillars

1. Collect. Keywords with volume and difficulty from a real, dated source, plus the questions people ask assistants.
2. Group by intent. Same need and largely the same results means one page. A different need or format means separate pages.
3. Choose pillars. Broad subjects with enough demand and enough distinct subtopics. Justify each in one line.
4. Build the tree. Hub → pillar → topic cluster → article. The hub orients, the pillar answers its subject alone and leads to depth, the cluster sums up a sub-intent, the article answers one precise question. Every page gets a level and a template
5. Assign. Every keyword and every question gets exactly one owner page, or a reasoned "deferred" or "out of scope". More on this one in the next part.
6. Link. Pillar to articles and back, articles to siblings, bridges between pillars, descriptive anchors. That internal linking is what tells Google how the pages relate.
7. Prioritise. Order the writing by demand, difficulty and what you can add.

![原文配图](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-正文-009-1.jpg)

Focus more closely on the editorial hierarchy links within 1 Pillar.

Two rules hold throughout: never invent a metric (a missing value is not zero), and the tree is finished only when every significant query has a page or a reasoned decision.

![原文配图](../../90_附件/GEO国外近期实操_20261028第三批_配图/2107445937698197617-正文-011-1.jpg)

Focus more closely on the internal links within 1 Pillar.

## Fill a page sheet before writing

Before an agent writes a word, it fills six lines:

- Target: main keyword, variants, owned questions.
- Reader's task: "For \[reader\], this page lets them \[task\]."
- Answer: the answer in one or two sentences.
- Unique information: what only this page brings. Your data, a sourced figure, a worked example, a tested method.
- Blocks: one line per block of the page's template.
- Links: parent, deeper pages, next action.

The line agents skip if you let them is unique information. For us it's IZeat's own sourced nutrition data per 100 g, something a reader can't get on the next result.

## Fill each block with one rule

The template says which blocks a page has. The method gives one rule per kind of block, whatever the page:

- Title, H1, description, URL: the subject and promise of this query. Nothing promised that the page doesn't deliver.
- Opening (standfirst, first paragraph or definition): answers the main question at once. A definition must read correctly if it's quoted alone.
- H2 and H3: the reader's sub-questions, in order.
- Unique information: source, date and scope beside every figure.

# Not ranking? Your pages may be fighting each other. How to stop it

When two of your pages answer the same search, Google has to pick one, and often ranks neither well. SEOs call it cannibalisation. With AI agents it happens fast: two agents, on two different days, will happily write two pages for the same query, and both will look fine on their own.

The rule that stops it is step 5: one owner page per keyword and per question. No page answers what another page owns.

Three things make the rule hold:

- A single table of owners. Every keyword has one row and one page. Ours is a shared spreadsheet; the agents read it before writing, and no other document copies it.
- A check that refuses duplicates. Each article declares its keywords, and a test fails when two articles declare the same one. The first time we ran it on our blog, it found 8 duplicates that had slipped in.
- One decision when it happens anyway. Two pages on the same query in Search Console: merge them, or split them by intent so each answers a different need.

# LLMs don't cite you? Your content isn't structured for them. The simple rules to follow

An assistant cuts a page into passages and quotes the one that answers. A passage that says "as seen above" can't be quoted. A table with units can.

| Need | Structure |
| --- | --- |
| Compare options, give quantities | A real table: units in the headers, one value per cell, source underneath, never an image |
| Explain a procedure | An ordered list, one action per step |
| List or sum up | A bulleted list, each item a sentence that stands alone |
| Give the facts of a term | A definition list: formula, unit, typical range, source |
| Answer a question | The question as a heading; its first sentence answers it |
| Every section | A self-contained passage that names its subject instead of "it" |

Then JSON-LD, which confused us longer than I'd like to admit. It's one block per page, in the head, describing the page and its main subject. Not one block per table.

Only a few visible blocks have a counterpart inside it: the FAQ (FAQPage), recipe steps (HowToStep), a nutrition table (NutritionInformation), a selection (ItemList), the breadcrumb (BreadcrumbList). Ordinary tables and lists have none. Engines read them from the HTML, which is exactly why their visible structure matters.

And the golden rule: JSON-LD describes only what is visible. No FAQPage without visible questions, no rating that doesn't exist. Google says no special markup is needed to appear in AI Overviews; the foundations are the same as for normal search.

# Still not ranking after all that? You may be following rules instead of readers

This is where I got it wrong. Two of the rules our agents followed came from our own design doc, and both claimed to copy Webflow: "a glossary entry is 250 words, like Webflow" and "two-sentence standfirst, the second sentence names IZeat". They were constraints copied from a famous site, not answers to what a reader needs. And an agent doesn't question a rule like that. It applies it 52 times.

So on 5 October, with free tools only and Claude driving Chrome, we counted.

| Glossary | Entries sampled | Median length | Opening |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Webflow | 100 | 134 words, no subheads | ~41 words |
| Ahrefs | 40 | ~600 words, with H2s | ~38 words |
| HubSpot | 40 | ~840 words | ~56 words |
| IZeat | — | ~258 words | — |

Webflow's glossary isn't 250 words. And there's no single right length: what the three share is a short opening that gives the definition first.

For article openings, Webflow's standfirst was one sentence in 49 of 60 posts (median 23 words), and its second sentence named Webflow once in 60. Healthline, Ahrefs, HubSpot and Zapier rarely use a standfirst; their first paragraph runs 26–34 words. Ours named IZeat in all 52 articles we had then, at a median of 59 words over two to four sentences. We had copied a pattern that didn't exist.

What replaced the two rules is the reader's need. The opening answers the question first. A page is as long as its question needs, no word count. The standfirst names IZeat only when IZeat helps answer the reader's question.

On the AEO side, a small sample in Google AI Overviews (4 questions, 13 cited pages): first paragraph around 47 words at the median, brand named early in only 3 of 13, about 1,000 words long. The type of page followed the question: calculators for "what is TDEE", listicles and app home pages for "best calorie counter app", recipe collections for "high protein meals".

Thirteen pages is a sample, not a law. What gets cited reflects today's competition: if nobody publishes structured, sourced data, its absence among citations proves nothing. One outside anchor points the same way as our decisions: the GEO paper (Aggarwal et al., KDD 2024) found that adding statistics, quotations and cited sources raised visibility in generative answers by roughly 22–41 %, while keyword stuffing didn't help. That was a controlled experiment on a research engine, not a measurement of any commercial assistant.

One more mistake, ours this time: the first version of our method file was 2,400 words, and I couldn't tell what it added. The rewrite came from three questions I kept asking: "what's the difference between this and the page template?", "why do we measure AEO and not SEO?", "is JSON-LD one per page or one per table?". It's about 1,400 words now.

Part 2 covers off-site: everything that happens outside your own website.

If you build with Claude Code or Codex: where does your agents' method live today?
